articles.title: Huang kallas till förhör efter spionuppgifter
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Huang kallas till förhör efter spionuppgifter
articles.body_text: Jensen Huang. Bild från hans senaste Stockholmsbesök, i mitten av oktober. Huang kallas till förhör efter spionuppgifter Nvidias vd kallas till utfrågningar i USA:s kongress, efter medieuppgifter om att han haft en relation med en befarad kinesisk spion. Bland andra Financial Times och The New York Times har, med hänvisning till källor, skrivit om att Nvidia-chefen Jensen Huang umgåtts med en kvinna som lett en av it-bjässens kunder. Efter artiklarna har tre utskott i USA:s representanthus begärt att Huang ska inställa sig den 18 november. Ämnet för utfrågningen beskrivs i kallelsen som ”Nvidias säkerhetsrutiner mot utländskt spionage och ert samröre med vad som rapporteras vara en kinesisk underrättelseperson”. USA har hårda kontroller visavi Kina för avancerad teknik, och uppges nu befara att kvinnan ingår i försök att påverka reglerna. Nvidia har tidigare avvisat misstankarna , och förklarat att det är fullt naturligt att Huang umgås med kunder.

articles.title: Barn blev appberoende – förlikas med techjätte
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Barn blev appberoende – förlikas med techjätte
articles.body_text: Två tonåringar anklagar Snap för att medvetet ha gjort dem beroende. Arkivbild. Barn blev appberoende – förlikas med techjätte Två tonåringar som anklagat Snapchat för att medvetet ha gjort dem beroende av appen har nått en förlikning med ägaren. Målet hade valts ut av en domstol i Kalifornien bland tusentals liknande fall. ”Vårt yttersta mål är att sociala medier-företagen ska stå till svars för hur deras agerande har påverkat miljontals barn i landet”, säger advokaten John Morgan, som företräder ungdomarna, i ett uttalande. Tonåringarna från Illinois och Mississippi började använda Youtube vid tre års ålder och andra appar när de var nio, enligt Reuters . De anklagar företagen för att ha skapat beroendeframkallande funktioner. Nu har de gjort upp med den börsnoterade techjätten Snap, efter att tidigare ha ingått förlikningar med Meta, Tiktok och Youtube. Snaps vd Evan Spiegel skulle vittna i domstolen i veckan, men i och med förlikningen undvek man vad som hade varit företagets första rättegång om Snapchats påverkan på unga. Samtidigt tillbakavisar Snap anklagelserna och hävdar att företaget vidtagit åtgärder för att göra apparna till ”trygga platser” där unga kan uttrycka sig. Fallet hade valts ut av Kaliforniens högsta domstol bland tusentals liknande fall. Meta och Youtube förlorade ett första sådant mål i delstaten i mars. En jury utdömde då 6 miljoner dollar i skadestånd till en ung kvinna. Nästa liknande fall kommer att inledas i mars, enligt Reuters .

articles.title: Paraguays president avsatt – kan åtalas
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Paraguays president avsatt – kan åtalas
articles.body_text: Santiago Peña skrev i torsdags under den avskedsansökan som på fredagen avvisades av landets senat. Paraguays senat har röstat för att avsätta president Santiago Peña till följd av misskötsel. Beslutet innebär att Peña kan komma att åtalas till följd av den bankkris som drabbat landet. Genom att avsätta Peña i stället för att acceptera den avskedsansökan som han lämnat in fråntas Peña möjligheten till en livslång plats i senaten och den immunitet som han annars enligt lag hade åtnjutit. Krisen utlöstes i samband med att banken Ueno – där ungefär 60 procent av landets vuxna är kunder – kollapsat, vilket skickade chockvågor genom landets finansiella system. Peña har tidigare varit delägare i den koncern som kontrollerar banken. Åklagare har inlett en utredning om Ueno-kraschen, där bland andra Peña är föremål för granskning. Enligt åklagare har Peña nu satts i husarrest. Vicepresidenten Pedro Alliana har svurits in som ny president.

articles.title: Spansk olivolja hålls tillbaka mot prisras
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Spansk olivolja hålls tillbaka mot prisras
articles.body_text: Spansk olivolja hålls tillbaka mot prisras För att stoppa ett kraftigt prisfall beordrar Spanien landets olivoljefabriker att hålla inne 12 procent av sin produktion, rapporterar Bloomberg. Beslutet, som presenterades av jordbruksminister Luis Planas Puchades under fredagen, innebär att cirka 188 000 ton olivolja tas bort från marknaden. Enligt EU:s och Spaniens bestämmelser kan sådana åtgärder tillåtas om det totala utbudet överstiger 120 procent av genomsnittet från de sex senaste säsongerna. Den stora skörden tillsammans med befintliga lager pressade priserna på extra jungfruolja till ett femårslägsta i slutet av oktober. Efter två år med svår torka, 2022 och 2023, har gynnsamt väder med mycket regn lett till ett kraftigt uppsving. Årets produktion beräknas öka med 23 procent till 1,6 miljoner ton – den fjärde största skörden någonsin i landet. Spanien står för en tredjedel av världens olivoljeproduktion.

articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: De gör upp om att bli ny ECB-chef
articles.body_text: Europeiska centralbankens kontor under en dimmig dag i Frankfurt. Arkivbild. Två kandidater har kastat in hatten i ringen för att efterträda Christine Lagarde som chef för Europeiska centralbanken ECB. Det är spanjoren Pablo Hernández de Cos och nederländaren Klaas Kno, som anmält sig till posten, meddelar eurogruppen i ett pressmeddelande . De är båda tidigare chefer för sina respektive länders centralbanker. Hernández de Cos är också sittande chef för centralbankernas egen bank, BIS. Förhoppningen är att ett beslut om vem som ersätter Lagarde, som avgår i förtid den 7 februari 2027, kan fattas i mitten av december, uppger en källa för nyhetsbyrån AFP.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Pope Leo in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
articles.summary: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.body_text: Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer. The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation. The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan. The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru , which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop. "I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay. "Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed. Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread. On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed. In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone". He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment. He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral. Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

articles.title: Jehovah's Witness rules on blood transfusions have changed, but it's too late for my brother
articles.summary: Jehovah's Witness leaders relaxed strict rules on blood transfusions, but the change came 23 days too late for Isaac Valdez.
articles.body_text: In August this year, 26-year-old Isaac Valdez had an epileptic seizure while browsing in his local library, causing him to convulse and strike his head against the ground. He lost consciousness. Later, in hospital, it transpired Isaac had hit his head with such force it had led to a brain haemorrhage. Treatment was seriously complicated by the fact that, as a Jehovah's Witness, Isaac carried a "No Blood" card, an indication that he would not accept treatment involving any form of blood transfusion because of his religious beliefs. As a result, a procedure to drain fluid from Isaac's brain did not take place. But his family, from Waxahachie, Texas, were encouraged by the fact that he regained consciousness and even started to talk again. He was able to confirm that he stood by his "no blood" beliefs. The family's relief at his apparent improvement was short-lived. Isaac slipped into a coma and his condition worsened rapidly. A neurosurgeon told Isaac's family the only way to save his life was an emergency operation, but that it was one that required blood transfusion. His family took the decision to abide by Issac's wishes as a lifelong Witness not to accept such a procedure. Isaac - who his twin brother Jacob Valdez describes as an intelligent man who loved volunteering and helping the elderly - died on 26 August 2026 when doctors turned off his life support. Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced a seismic change in teaching that would, in effect, have given Isaac the religious green light to have the life-saving treatment he had refused. The change suddenly means the vast majority of medical procedures using donated blood are no longer prohibited to followers. Now, decisions on whether to accept such treatments are to be left to individuals. Jacob, already dealing with the death of his twin, was angered at the Jehovah's Witnesses' leadership for not coming to their conclusion sooner. He told BBC News he believes Isaac could well still be alive if they had.

articles.title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and under house arrest
articles.summary: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.
articles.body_text: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts. Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests. He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents. Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing. The impeachment charges that led to Peña's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank. He is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said. Peña's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal. "Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank. Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday. An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, Asunción. Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

articles.title: With Stephen Miller pick, Trump readies for a battle
articles.summary: The US president's promotion of Miller, a loyal partisan firebrand to be his new chief of staff sets up likely clashes with Congress.
articles.body_text: In the aftermath of the Republican Party's sweeping defeat in Tuesday's midterm elections, Donald Trump said he would be willing to work with the newly ascendent Democrats in Congress. On Friday, however, he elevated Stephen Miller, his bare-knuckled political operative and longtime adviser, to replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff. Far from an olive branch to Congress, Miller's promotion could be a sign that the president is girding for political battle by installing a partisan firebrand in the top White House job. "The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our president and defend this magnificent republic," Miller posted on X, adding that he was "honored beyond words" to be Trump's pick for the job. One of the most powerful positions in Washington, the chief of staff is gatekeeper to the president, agenda-setter in the White House and chief negotiator with Congress and other outside political interests. "Stephen Miller's been with me since the beginning," Trump said in comments to reporters after announcing the move on his Truth Social website. "He gets it." Miller is best known for being the driving force behind the Trump administration's aggressive immigration enforcement policies, which has included ramping up funding for enforcement operations across the US. He made headlines when he called Alex Pretti, who was shot and killed by federal immigration officials during a massive deportation operation in Minneapolis, a "domestic terrorist" and an "assassin". He would later walk back those words, saying federal agents "may not have been following" proper protocol. He has also reportedly played a leading role in the US military operations in Venezuela and against suspected drug trafficking operations in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, which critics have condemned as extra-judicial killings. Miller joined Trump's political operation early in his 2016 presidential bid as a strategist and incendiary warm-up speaker at his raucous campaign rallies. He was one of the few senior White House staffers to persevere through the entirety of his first term. He stayed loyal to Trump during his political exile following attempts to overturn his ballot-box defeat in 2020 failed. He then returned in the influential role of deputy chief of staff for policy in Trump's second term. Wiles, who co-managed the president's successful 2024 re-election campaign, developed a reputation as a cool professional who avoided the White House staffing upheavals, dramatic policy reversals and personality clashes that typified Trump's first presidential term.

articles.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
articles.summary: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.
articles.body_text: European Union prosecutors have begun investigating the possible misuse of EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people last week. Prosecutors backed by a special unit of Spain's Guardia Civil security force said they were conducting the inquiry at the offices of Adif rail infrastructure authority and rail safety agency AESF. The 28 October accident on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line was one of the worst railway disasters in Europe this century. It is the second EU fraud inquiry opened into Spain's railways this year, after 46 people were killed on the same line at Adamuz in January. Last week, a train operated by state-owned operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo outside the village of Urda, around 130km (80 miles) south of Madrid. The LZB communication system that monitors the position of trains had gone down, and the Renfe train had been given the all clear to start running at normal speed, even though the Iryo train ahead of it had been unable to restart. The two accidents nine months apart on the same line have claimed 115 lives and dozens more injuries. The European Public Prosecutor's Office (EPPO) said on Friday it had begun conducting investigative measures at Spain's rail authorities "after the opening of an investigation into possible fraud affecting EU funds allocated to the renovation and upgrading of safety, signalling and communications systems on the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line". The EPPO highlighted high public interest in the case, but said no further details would be made public. As part of the process, a Spanish judge assigned to the case has to ensure the investigation complies with legal safeguards, including authorising any measures that might involve house searches or phone-tapping. The Urda disaster has damaged the Socialist-led government of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez ahead of a 29 November general election and the party is trailing the conservative People's Party (PP) in most opinion polls. Close Sánchez ally Óscar Puente resigned this week as transport minister, after seeing two deadly accidents on his watch this year.

articles.title: Four midterms takeaways for 2028 White House race
articles.summary: The buzz about the presidential election is already under way - here's what we learned this week.
articles.body_text: Ballots are still being counted in the US midterm elections but the political landscape is already pivoting to the 2028 White House race. Buoyed by major gains in Congress, Democrats will have momentum as they prepare for the contest to succeed President Donald Trump. But a good showing in the midterms does not guarantee a White House win two years later. Barack Obama was re-elected in 2012 despite huge Republican gains in 2010. No one has yet entered the presidential race but potential candidates will be preparing behind the scenes. Vice-President's JD Vance's reflection on where the midterms went wrong for Republicans has been interpreted as him paving the way for a 2028 run. The results of Tuesday's election and the historic size of Democratic gains could shape the White House race in several ways. Here are four takeaways. Several prominent potential presidential candidates were running in the 2026 midterms - and some emerged looking strong. Georgia Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff won by a sizeable margin in the politically competitive state that Trump won in 2024. While he has previously said he has no plans to run for president, his successful campaign, with several viral moments, helped boost his national profile. Another potential Democratic nominee, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro , swept aside his Republican challenger. Shapiro has not committed to a 2028 run but analysts point to his broad appeal in swing-state Pennsylvania as a sign that he could be competitive on the national stage. Illinois Governor JB Pritzker also won after a campaign pundits in his state described as a "tune-up" for a presidential run.

articles.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
articles.summary: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.
articles.body_text: European airlines have again been hit with a new wave of bomb threats - in the third such incident this week. On Friday multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted and the threats saw three planes escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, authorities said. It also saw a number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ , evacuated after threats were made against them - although there has been no concrete links between the messages against airlines and the broadcasters. The disruption comes after nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted by threats earlier this week , in what the UK called a "malicious hoax". A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP. France also reported at least four of its flights were targeted by threats, however they all landed safely. No explosives have been found on any planes as of Friday. As airlines were dealing with this latest wave of threats, several media outlets, including RTÉ, were evacuated after similar warnings were made against them. Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and the Dublin offices of radio stations NewstalkFM and TodayFM, were also advised to leave their buildings and UK broadcaster Sky said it also received a security threat. In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe". While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption". In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort.

articles.title: AI stocks bounce back after trillions wiped from market values
articles.summary: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.
articles.body_text: Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have recovered slightly from an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index closed in positive territory following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, ending the day up 1.1%, partly reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, closed up 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day before ending slightly down 0.4%. Companies that lost hundreds of billions in market value recovered some ground on Friday, including Nvidia, SpaceX and Tesla. However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse. The Kospi in South Korea closed down 6% on Friday, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix plunging more than 10%. European markets also fell, with the main indexes in Germany, France and Spain ending the day down. In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%. In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices.

articles.title: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
articles.summary: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.
articles.body_text: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has said production of the firm's Cybertruck is "winding down" in Texas, to focus on its self-driving Cybercab cars. The model is only produced at Tesla's Austin base, and he did not clarify if manufacturing would be moved elsewhere or simply cease. The Cybertruck has received a mixed response since its launch in 2023, with some praising its individuality and others simply labelling it ugly. It has also suffered from disappointing sales, quality problems and recalls. BBC technology reporter Shiona McCallum has this report. The BBC's technology correspondent Joe Tidy explains how it happened, and what it means for you. Social media giant Meta is on trial over claims it deliberately designed its platforms to be addictive to young people. The prime minister announced that under-16s will be banned from social media by spring 2027. The BBC's Vanessa Clarke talks through the government's new advice for children using screens. Some major retailers and independent stores have introduced AI body scans, CCTV or facial recognition equipment to identify crimes like shoplifting. The BBC's Asia business correspondent says it is still unclear what sort of experience TikTok users in the US will get. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has been named game of the year at this year's Game Awards.

articles.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
articles.summary: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.
articles.body_text: A young girl and an 18-year-old man have died after a bus crashed in eastern France, local authorities have said. The bus was travelling between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse when it crashed at around 07:00 local time on Friday in the town of Lent. The bus was carrying 43 passengers, including 15 children, the Bourg-en-Bresse prosecutor's office said. Three people are in a critical condition and at least 13 others have sustained minor injuries. French President Emmanuel Macron said his thoughts were with the victims, the injured, and their families. In a post on X, he said the nation stood by their side and thanked the rescue teams involved. The town's mayor Yves Cristin told French media the bus "left the road and hit a tree in the ditch". The two people killed have been identified by authorities. However, there have been differing reports as to the age of the girl. The prosecutor's office said it was "opening an investigation into the incident, on charges of road homicide and aggravated road traffic injuries". The driver has been taken to hospital after sustaining injuries and has not yet been questioned by police. French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said initial tests indicated there were no traces of alcohol or drugs in his blood. Photos circulating in French media show a blue and white bus tilted in what appears to be a ditch on the roadside. Trees line the side of the road. The front of the bus appears to be heavily damaged. Local mayor Cristin told BFM TV: "I arrived minutes after the accident and people were in shock. "The side of the bus was torn off, and clearly, the people who were on that side must have been seriously injured."

articles.title: Paul Mackenzie: Kenya doomsday cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison for Shakahola deaths
articles.summary: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".
articles.body_text: A Kenyan court has sentenced the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children. Alongside 28 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus". Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie bore the "primary criminal culpability" for ordering his followers to fast to death, in one of the world's deadliest episodes of cult activity. "The sentence is appropriate and just, to send an unmistakable message that such atrocities warrant the maximum penalties allowed by law," the judge added. The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast. The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention. The court sentenced Mackenzie to 100 years in prison for homicide and another 100 years for offences related to starvation. The sentences within each category will run concurrently, but the two sets will run consecutively, bringing his total prison term to 200 years. Mackenzie also faces separate manslaughter and terrorism charges, which he denies. Prosecutors had sought the death penalty, arguing that the scale and circumstances of the killings warranted the harshest punishment. However, Justice Mochache declined to impose the death penalty, despite ruling that the case met the threshold for its consideration. "Nevertheless, the court declines the invitation to impose the death penalty on any of the victims," she said, adding that capital punishment would eliminate any prospect of rehabilitation and disengagement. The death sentence has not been carried out in Kenya since 1987. Mackenzie was tried alongside 28 accomplices, including guards who enforced his fasting orders and gravediggers who helped conceal the victims' bodies in mass graves.

articles.title: Judge blocks construction of Donald Trump's massive arch
articles.summary: The Trump administration had hoped the construction of the 250-foot arch could begin as early as this week.
articles.body_text: A federal judge has temporarily blocked construction of US President Donald Trump's "triumphal arch" in the nation's capital. US District Judge Tanya Chutkan ruled that there should be a 14-day pause before any work can start on the arch in Washington which the Trump administration had said could begin this week. Earlier on Thursday the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC) voted 8-4 to allow construction of the planned 250ft (72m) arch. Trump appointees on the board said the arch would be a fitting tribute to US history and to veterans but opponents have argued it would block the view of Arlington National Cemetery, the resting place of thousands of US soldiers and service people. The so-called Arc de Trump - a play on the name of the famous arch in Paris, the Arc de Triomphe - is one of the president's efforts to remake the capital city in his style and is meant to commemorate the country's 250th anniversary. The approval on Thursday evening came after nearly nine hours of public comment. "The White House commends the National Capital Planning Commission's decision to fully approve President Trump's historic vision to build a much needed Triumphal Arch in Washington, DC," a White House spokesperson told the BBC in a statement. It is not yet clear when construction of the arch could begin, as several lawsuits seek to block the project. The White House criticised the federal court that temporarily halted construction as an "activist district court." "We are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds and look forward to seeing the completion of this magnificent Arch," the spokesperson said. A rendering of the project's design from earlier this year includes a golden, winged Lady Liberty statue on the top of the arch, flanked by two gold eagles. The phrases "One Nation Under God" and "Liberty and Justice for All" are inscribed in gold on either side of the structure. A website that the White House shared on social media on Friday also shows a video rendering of the arch that shows the structure emblazoned with the words "Golden Age of America" along one side.

articles.title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
articles.summary: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.
articles.body_text: More than 20 aircraft across Europe have been targeted by bomb threats. It's the second time this week, which the UK has called a "malicious hoax". BBC Verify has been analysing the messages sent by an aircraft to find out what happens when a flight receives a bomb hoax - as Thomas Copeland explains. Additional reporting by Emma Pengelly. Produced by Aisha Sembhi. Graphics by Mesut Ersoz and Sally Nicholls. US immigration agencies posted images of people they say were arrested for illegally voting in US elections. President Trump has claimed in the past that non-citizen voting is “rampant” - but studies suggest proven cases are extremely rare. A private jet crashed in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board, according to US authorities. BBC Verify goes to an election centre to get a behind-the-scenes look at how mail-in ballots for the US midterm elections are processed. BBC Verify has pieced together defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro's journey through Brazil, Argentina and Ecuador to reach Miami. BBC Verify has tracked dozens of AI ads to assess how they are being used by campaigns in the midterms. Texas Democrat James Talarico was missing from the Senate campaign trail for nine days and said he had flu. Some conservative influencers falsely claimed he was receiving treatment at an Ohio mental health facility, but footage showed him at a festival in Texas at the time. Rules on the recording and filming of executions differ between state, federal and military regulations. The US aircraft carrier was set to return in May but the war with Iran has kept it at sea on one of the longest deployments ever. The death penalty is back in the news after Christa Pike survived two lethal injection attempts in Tennessee - but how widely used is it in the US?

articles.title: Was an Italian chef really fired over pineapple on pizza row?
articles.summary: The chef had stated that putting pineapple on pizza was "offensive to his culture".
articles.body_text: Italian chef Davide Tamburella was fired from a Brisbane restaurant in May after the establishment's management expressed concerns about a string of complaints about the chef's behaviour. Among them were Tamburella's refusal to provide ham and pineapple pizza for guests at a function. It was the third time Tamburella had refused to use the fruit on pizzas in the past four years. At the time, the chef had stated that putting pineapple on pizza was "offensive to his culture". Australia correspondent Katy Watson explains what led to Tamburella's dismissal. Read more about Davide Tamburella's story. The BBC’s Katy Watson explains why triple-murderer Erin Patterson is back in court this week trying to overturn her conviction. The humpback whale later successfully freed itself after the tide rose in Queensland, Australia. A police pursuit in Queensland has ended in two arrests, with authorities taken on a high-speed car chase across Ipswich and Brisbane. Seven-year-old Miles Phillips' hit song has now had 1.5m views and was even played on the radio. Five episodes of the award-winning children’s cartoon have been released in Australian Indigenous language for the first time. The five-year-old elephant seal attracted global attention during his recent time ashore in southern Tasmania.

articles.title: Balance de los primeros 100 días del gobierno de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori
articles.summary: Diversos líderes empresariales de la Confiep y de sus gremios asociados nos dan su opinión tras los 100 días de la presidenta Fujimori.
articles.body_text: Estos 100 días han mostrado planes y algunas acciones concretas. Enfrentar la delincuencia y el crimen organizado, y un fenómeno de El Niño extraordinario como el que viene, son sin duda temas prioritarios. Debemos incluir en la agenda esfuerzos dirigidos a implementar las grandes reformas económicas y de gobernanza que el país requiere. Valoramos los esfuerzos por recuperar la estabilidad política y sostener el dinamismo económico. Urgen resultados en seguridad ciudadana, infraestructura vial y transporte público. No podemos seguir postergando soluciones a problemas que llevan años frenando nuestro desarrollo. El Perú necesita decisiones firmes. Durante estos primeros 100 días de gobierno se ha percibido un ánimo positivo en los consumidores, lo que viene ayudando al dinamismo del negocio en los centros comerciales. El tema pendiente se ha centrado en la demora y recorte de las facultades que solicitó el Gobierno al Congreso. Se esperaba una actitud más constructiva por parte de la oposición. Desde la ACP valoramos el diálogo con el ministro de Salud e impulso a la transformación digital en estos 100 días. Hoy son prioridades la articulación público-privada ante El Niño, el desembalse quirúrgico y el primer nivel, y una coproducción regulatoria que elimine normas obsoletas. A 100 días de gobierno, valoramos la importancia de generar condiciones para la inversión y el crecimiento. Desde el sector aéreo, creemos fundamental avanzar en soluciones que reduzcan los sobrecostos que afectan la conectividad y coordinar medidas de prevención y respuesta frente a los impactos del fenómeno de El Niño. En estos primeros 100 días de gobierno destacamos que la infraestructura sea una prioridad para el desarrollo del país. Desde Afin, promovemos inversiones que cierren brechas, generen empleo y mejoren la competitividad. Para avanzar, es clave acelerar proyectos, simplificar trámites y garantizar seguridad jurídica, con colaboración público-privada y APP que mejoren los servicios públicos. Es importante que el Gobierno haya mostrado la situación en que recibió el Estado y actúe frente al FEN y la criminalidad. Sin embargo, es urgente que acelere la reforma del Estado, reduzca la burocracia, elimine la regulación inútil, fortalezca la seguridad jurídica y la competitividad para atraer inversiones. El Perú debe crecer 6% para generar más empleo y bienestar. Desde Alafarpe saludamos la apertura al diálogo con los actores del sistema al cumplirse 100 días de gestión. Es fundamental mantener esta articulación para construir una agenda compartida y enfocada en la salud y el bienestar de los peruanos en todas las regiones del país. La salud es un ejemplo de un tema común de estos 100 primeros días: los problemas los tienen las personas, pero es tanto el gobierno como el Congreso a quien les corresponde intentar resolverlos. La gente sabe que son complejos, pero se necesita ver la dirección correcta, ganas de pisar callos y priorizar a las personas. Martin Naranjo, presidente de la Asociación de Bancos del Perú (Asbanc) En estos primeros 100 días se abre un nuevo capítulo para el Perú. Es muy positivo que el fenómeno de El Niño esté en el centro de la agenda nacional. En ese marco, los líderes de todos los sectores pueden contribuir a fortalecer la unidad y la coordinación necesarias para afrontar mejor sus posibles efectos. En estos primeros 100 días, saludo que la reforma previsional avance con medidas como la pensión mínima. El reto es ampliar la cobertura ante la alta informalidad laboral. Desde la Aseaf, apoyamos iniciativas que fortalezcan el ahorro y permitan otorgar pensiones que brinden bienestar. En estos primeros 100 días de gobierno, el gremio cementero reafirma su compromiso de trabajar de la mano con el Estado para enfrentar el cambio climático, impulsar la descarbonización y la economía circular, y construir juntos un Perú más sostenible. Valoramos el inicio de la convocatoria de Compras a MYPErú y el anuncio de medidas para que la micro y pequeña empresa (mype) afronte el fenómeno de El Niño. Se deben implementar mecanismos excepcionales para evitar el rompimiento de la cadena de pagos. La tarea pendiente está en frenar la extorsión que afecta a todos los pequeños negocios Desde el sector seguros tenemos herramientas para mejorar la respuesta frente a las emergencias climáticas que estamos por enfrentar. El gobierno puede utilizar la potencia de seguros paramétricos para financiar la atención, proveer respuesta más oportuna y no generar desequilibrios presupuestales. El Gobierno ha puesto en agenda reformas necesarias para el país, pero el gran desafío sigue siendo pasar a la ejecución. La atención de El Niño añade una urgencia: proteger a la población y asegurar la continuidad de la actividad productiva. Para el mercado de capitales, concretar la Entidad de Contrapartida Central en el Perú contribuirá a fortalecer su infraestructura, generar confianza y atraer más inversión de largo plazo. La expectativa del sector inmobiliario es positiva, con una meta de 1’250,000 viviendas en el plan de gobierno. Sin embargo, preocupa el agotamiento de recursos del Fondo Mivivienda para vivienda social y la falta de previsión ante esta situación. Urge corregirla para no afectar a un sector clave para el crecimiento del PBI y el segundo que mayor inversión privada moviliza. Valoramos las medidas anunciadas en seguridad y frente a El Niño. Pero urge avanzar en reformas que destraben inversiones, promuevan el empleo formal y mejoren el Estado. Los primeros 100 días son un punto de partida. Ahora toca convertir las promesas en resultados. Y que el Congreso se sume. El balance es moderadamente positivo por la estabilidad macroeconómica y las expectativas de inversión. Sin embargo, persisten desafíos en seguridad ciudadana, ejecución de proyectos y formalización laboral. El reto es convertir los anuncios en resultados concretos que impulsen el crecimiento. Reconocemos la voluntad del gobierno de abordar temas vinculados a la mejora del marco regulatorio del sector minero energético y la preparación del país frente a la emergencia por el fenómeno de El Niño. En este último caso, es importante ampliar los esfuerzos ya mostrados para garantizar la continuidad de los servicios básicos como la electricidad, así como los combustibles a los peruanos. El gobierno ha presentado su proyecto de Ley Mape que esperamos sea un punto de partida para que la actividad minera en toda la cadena y de cualquier estrato se trabaje de manera formal, con estándares de respeto ambiental y de seguridad. Si bien el texto normativo tiene aspectos de mejora esperamos ver en las siguientes semanas mecanismos efectivos de control y fiscalización, así como una lucha frontal contra la minería ilegal. En los primeros 100 días del gobierno, en el sector pesquero destacamos el fortalecimiento del Imarpe y de la investigación científica, así como la articulación público-privada. Están pendientes las medidas concretas del gobierno para mitigar el impacto del FEN con miras a proteger el empleo y preservar las capacidades de la cadena productiva pesquera.

articles.title: Presidente de Paraguay no acude al Senado y delega a sus abogados para presentar defensa
articles.summary: Santiago Peña deberá acudir al Senado paraguayo para ejercer su defensa en el proceso de juicio político, luego de que rechazaran su pedido de más tiempo.
articles.body_text: Los abogados del presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, acudieron este viernes al Senado para presentar la defensa “técnica” y “jurídica” del mandatario en el juicio político iniciado en su contra, que, pese a haber sido convocado en persona para comparecer ante el Legislativo, no asistió y delegó por ahora su representación, en medio del escándalo desatado por el cierre del privado Ueno Bank. Los letrados, Adolfo Ferreiro y Ricardo Preda, llegaron al pleno cerca de las 13.00 horas locales (16.00 GMT) y tras el rechazo del Senado al pedido de prórroga de 72 horas solicitado por Peña para ejercer su defensa. Peña, quien permanece formalmente en el cargo después de que el Congreso no se pronunció por falta de cuórum sobre la renuncia que presentó la víspera, había advertido poco antes que las 12 horas establecidas por el Senado para preparar su estrategia eran insuficientes. Paraguay atraviesa por una crisis política después de que el Banco Central (BCP) ordenó un proceso de resolución o cierre de Ueno bank, una institución que durante la gestión de Peña recibió millonarios recursos de entidades públicas. El BCP detectó que el índice de solvencia del banco, que controlaba los recursos de más de 2,9 millones de clientes, había caído por debajo del 50 % del mínimo exigido, “como consecuencia de ajustes realizados a sus estados financieros durante el proceso de regularización”. articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

Santiago Peña es detenido en Paraguay tras ser destituido por el Congreso en un juicio político
articles.summary: El expresidente Santiago Peña permanecerá detenido en su domicilio y deberá comparecer este sábado ante la Fiscalía de Paraguay, que lo investiga por presunta lesión de confianza, tráfico de influencias y administración en provecho propio, tras el escándalo Ueno Bank
articles.body_text: El Senado de Paraguay destituyó este viernes al presidente Santiago Peña, quien poco después terminó detenido en su residencia a raíz de la caída de Ueno Bank, una entidad con la que el ahora exmandatario es vinculado y a la que fueron a parar durante su gestión millonarios fondos de entidades estatales. Lo que comenzó el pasado martes con una publicación en X del Banco Central del Paraguay (BCP) comunicando el inicio de un proceso de resolución, o disolución, fue tornándose en una tormenta a medida que angustiados clientes se acercaban a las sucursales del banco para preguntar por sus recursos, desde entonces congelados. La medida, según la entidad emisora, se adoptó tras constatarse que el índice de Ueno estaba por debajo del 50 % del mínimo requerido “como consecuencia de ajustes realizados a sus estados financieros” durante un proceso de regularización al que fue sometido. El desenlace se vivió este viernes, en la segunda jornada de un juicio político impulsado por diputados de oposición y disidentes del oficialismo, cuando con el voto de los 44 senadores presentes, en su mayoría antiguos correligionarios suyos, Peña fue declarado culpable por “mal desempeño de funciones” y, en consecuencia, destituido. La votación, que transcurrió en ausencia del acusado, quien delegó su representación en dos abogados, convirtió a Peña, de 47 años, en el segundo presidente en la historia reciente del país en ser desalojado del poder mediante un juicio político, después del izquierdista Fernando Lugo (2008-2012). Peña permanecía en el cargo después de que el Congreso no se pronunció por falta de cuórum sobre la renuncia que presentó el jueves. Desde entonces, el debate se centró en la conveniencia de su salida por dimisión o destitución. El artículo 189 de la Constitución establece que los expresidentes elegidos democráticamente serán senadores vitalicios, “salvo que hubiesen sido sometidos a juicio político y hallados culpables”. Un senador vitalicio goza de fueros y no puede ser sometido a un proceso penal sin que se apruebe en el Congreso el retiro de dicha inmunidad. Con la destitución, Peña no será senador vitalicio, lo que dejó el camino abierto para someterlo a la Justicia. El ahora exmandatario fue incluido por la Fiscalía en una investigación por Ueno Bank y otra serie de hechos denunciados por legisladores. Fue así como se libró una orden de detención, que poco después del juicio la hizo efectiva la Policía, cuando acudió a la residencia de Peña, donde permanecerá antes de comparecer mañana a una audiencia. Los hallazgos del BCP confirmaron lo que meses atrás advertían expertos y diputados de oposición en torno a Ueno, mientras el entonces jefe de Estado abogaba por la institución. El impacto y el malestar crecieron a medida que se conocían las cifras. Dos de cada tres paraguayos, tal como señala la web del banco, tenían cuenta en esa entidad, entre ellos 32.000 de un total de 91.000 jubilados del Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS), que recibían sus pensiones cada mes. El IPS, que invirtió 355 millones de dólares en la entidad, es una de las cinco cajas jubilatorias que confiaron sus fondos en una institución que el Banco Central “mató”, ya que “no tenía remedio”, aseguró este viernes la diputada Rocío Vallejo, al presentar los alegatos finales del juicio. La legisladora subrayó que Peña “creó un agujero de 1.200 millones de dólares al pueblo paraguayo” y “tres millones de perjudicados en un solo día”, en alusión al proceso de resolución, por lo que se refirió al ahora exgobernante como “el desfalcador más grande de la historia del Paraguay”. La destitución activó la sucesión en el Ejecutivo, que pasó a manos del hasta hoy vicepresidente, Pedro Alliana, quien juró en una sesión extraordinaria del Congreso. Ejercerá el cargo hasta agosto de 2028, cuando concluye el periodo actual de Gobierno. Luego fue juramentado como vicepresidente Antonio Barrios, elegido senador en 2023 y médico personal del titular del Partido Colorado, el exmandatario Horacio Cartes. “Lo que vengo a prometer es concreto: los compatriotas que hoy atraviesan un momento difícil a consecuencia del descalabro financiero serán compensados plenamente. No los vamos a dejar solos”, anunció el nuevo gobernante en su primer discurso, en el que anticipó que “ya se hizo suficiente en el exterior”, en aparente alusión a los criticados viajes de Peña, y prometió recortar “los gastos superfluos”. Entretanto, la Fiscalía ha reportado la incautación de bienes como avionetas, vehículos de lujo y abundante documentación en los allanamientos a Ueno y las empresas de Ueno Holding, en las que Peña tuvo acciones hasta marzo de 2025, según la acusación. También hoy un juez envió a cárceles de procesados a uno de los fundadores de Ueno, Miguel Vázquez, y otros cinco directivos. Por su parte, la Asociación de Importadores y Comerciantes del Paraguay (Asimcopar) reportó que las ventas en las tiendas y multitiendas ha caído hasta un 70 % tras el cierre de Ueno, y el BCP debió sacar antes al mercado los nuevos billetes de 100.000 guaraníes ante la inusual demanda de efectivo.

articles.title: Presidente de Paraguay no acude al Senado y delega a sus abogados para presentar defensa
articles.summary: Santiago Peña deberá acudir al Senado paraguayo para ejercer su defensa en el proceso de juicio político, luego de que rechazaran su pedido de más tiempo.
articles.body_text: Los abogados del presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, acudieron este viernes al Senado para presentar la defensa “técnica” y “jurídica” del mandatario en el juicio político iniciado en su contra, que, pese a haber sido convocado en persona para comparecer ante el Legislativo, no asistió y delegó por ahora su representación, en medio del escándalo desatado por el cierre del privado Ueno Bank. Los letrados, Adolfo Ferreiro y Ricardo Preda, llegaron al pleno cerca de las 13.00 horas locales (16.00 GMT) y tras el rechazo del Senado al pedido de prórroga de 72 horas solicitado por Peña para ejercer su defensa. Peña, quien permanece formalmente en el cargo después de que el Congreso no se pronunció por falta de cuórum sobre la renuncia que presentó la víspera, había advertido poco antes que las 12 horas establecidas por el Senado para preparar su estrategia eran insuficientes. Paraguay atraviesa por una crisis política después de que el Banco Central (BCP) ordenó un proceso de resolución o cierre de Ueno bank, una institución que durante la gestión de Peña recibió millonarios recursos de entidades públicas. El BCP detectó que el índice de solvencia del banco, que controlaba los recursos de más de 2,9 millones de clientes, había caído por debajo del 50 % del mínimo exigido, “como consecuencia de ajustes realizados a sus estados financieros durante el proceso de regularización”. El jefe de Estado, señalado por sus vínculos con Ueno, terminó salpicado por la crisis y la víspera dimitió. Sin embargo, Peña permanece formalmente en la Presidencia de Paraguay ya que legisladores oficialistas dejaron sin cuórum la sesión conjunta convocada para votar su renuncia y así poder activar el mecanismo de sucesión tras declarar la vacancia del cargo. Si fuera destituido por el Parlamento, Peña perdería los fueros de senador vitalicio, que conservaría con la renuncia. Precisamente eso es lo que no quiere el Congreso, que lo convocó de manera inmediata al Senado, que actúa como juez, para el juicio político en el que está previsto que lo destituya.

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Presidente de Paraguay no acude al Senado y delega a sus abogados para presentar defensa
articles.summary: Santiago Peña deberá acudir al Senado paraguayo para ejercer su defensa en el proceso de juicio político, luego de que rechazaran su pedido de más tiempo.
articles.body_text: Los abogados del presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, acudieron este viernes al Senado para presentar la defensa “técnica” y “jurídica” del mandatario en el juicio político iniciado en su contra, que, pese a haber sido convocado en persona para comparecer ante el Legislativo, no asistió y delegó por ahora su representación, en medio del escándalo desatado por el cierre del privado Ueno Bank. Los letrados, Adolfo Ferreiro y Ricardo Preda, llegaron al pleno cerca de las 13.00 horas locales (16.00 GMT) y tras el rechazo del Senado al pedido de prórroga de 72 horas solicitado por Peña para ejercer su defensa. Peña, quien permanece formalmente en el cargo después de que el Congreso no se pronunció por falta de cuórum sobre la renuncia que presentó la víspera, había advertido poco antes que las 12 horas establecidas por el Senado para preparar su estrategia eran insuficientes. Paraguay atraviesa por una crisis política después de que el Banco Central (BCP) ordenó un proceso de resolución o cierre de Ueno bank, una institución que durante la gestión de Peña recibió millonarios recursos de entidades públicas. El BCP detectó que el índice de solvencia del banco, que controlaba los recursos de más de 2,9 millones de clientes, había caído por debajo del 50 % del mínimo exigido, “como consecuencia de ajustes realizados a sus estados financieros durante el proceso de regularización”. El jefe de Estado, señalado por sus vínculos con Ueno, terminó salpicado por la crisis y la víspera dimitió. Sin embargo, Peña permanece formalmente en la Presidencia de Paraguay ya que legisladores oficialistas dejaron sin cuórum la sesión conjunta convocada para votar su renuncia y así poder activar el mecanismo de sucesión tras declarar la vacancia del cargo. Si fuera destituido por el Parlamento, Peña perdería los fueros de senador vitalicio, que conservaría con la renuncia. Precisamente eso es lo que no quiere el Congreso, que lo convocó de manera inmediata al Senado, que actúa como juez, para el juicio político en el que está previsto que lo destituya.

articles.title: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sequoia pioneered the scouts model and many VC firms followed suit, but a consensus now seems to be forming that the model has reached limits in its current form.
articles.body_text: Sequoia this week announced a broad overhaul in a memo posted to X, a move that includes closing its London office and shutting down its scout program. Observers warn that it would be a mistake to read too much into the London closure, since the British capital has a thriving AI scene. On the other hand, the decision to end scouts says more about where venture investing is headed. That’s partly because 17 years ago, Sequoia pioneered the scouts model, in which select founders and operators write checks on the firm’s behalf. Amid increased competition for deal flow, many VC firms followed suit . But a consensus now seems to be emerging that the model has reached its limits in its current form. Not everyone was sold on the model in the first place. “They pioneered the scout program but [to be honest] it never made sense to me!” VC Sheel Mohnot wrote on X this week. “The scouts themselves don’t really care that much about the investments, you can still miss (like they did with Uber), not sure what it gets you. I suspect other firms will shutter theirs too.” he added. To be clear, Sequoia didn’t make a case against scouts in the memo. Instead, it framed its decision as part of a broader need for more focus. But its goal of “putting more energy behind fewer people and things” is likely to resonate with others who’ve questioned the ‘spray and pray’ approach to scouting. Rival firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), for instance, rolled out a global scout network aimed at spotting opportunities in the U.S. and also in smaller European hubs. But a16z partner Gabriel Vasquez told TechCrunch earlier this year that the firm had revamped its program to double down “on the best people.” Under this new approach, Vasquez explained, scouts get more resources but are also expected to be more active, such as by co-hosting dinners with the firm. “They get more budget, but we have reduced the number,” he said. This also seems to indicate that it is VC firms that have been driving an overhaul of the model. For founders, being a scout is attractive: it brings them closer to firms they may want checks from someday, or even a partner role with, and being seen as someone who can write a check can raise their standing among other founders. Some scouts will undoubtedly mourn the end of Sequoia’s program. Among them is Station F boss Roxanne Varza, who wrote on LinkedIn that she was “sad” to hear that the program was getting cut off, and “hope[d] that other funds [w]on’t follow suit.” Varza, a former Sequoia scout from 2020 to 2025, told TechCrunch that she had no information beyond what has been shared publicly, but observed that becoming a scout had often been a stepping stone for aspiring investment managers. “I cannot name all of the incredible scouts that have gone on to join or build funds, but there are quite a few. And the scout programs may have helped them get there — allowed them to build an investment track record, allowed them to build relationships with various funds directly, and more,” she wrote to TechCrunch. According to Varza, the program’s impact went beyond the individual level, instead helping the entire ecosystem become more mature. “I believe they have helped to foster the investment culture and early-stage investment landscape that we now see in Europe, for example,” Varza said. While others may agree with Varza about the role these programs have played, they may still have run their course for two reasons. First, seasoned operators may get more financial upside as angels. When it’s their own money, they get to keep the returns, too. Second, leading VC firms are now big and well-known enough that the best founders tend to come to them, so they worry less about missing deals, except at the very earliest stages or in niches and geographies where they have less reach.

articles.title: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.
articles.body_text: Right before the midterm elections, OpenAI hired Jessica Schumer , daughter of Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer. The company also said it would start calling its data centers “ compute campuses .” For the past two years, many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names have built closer ties with President Donald Trump and his administration. Several attended White House events, some companies scaled back diversity, equity and inclusion programs, and some executives donated millions to super PACs supporting his campaign and allied candidates. Administration policies also benefited the industry, including tax breaks, the pausing of some federal investigations, and looser AI regulation. Meanwhile, Meta faced lawsuits and billion-dollar fines, and OpenAI faced suits alleging its technology harmed users. Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI. How far that gets them may depend less on image-polishing than on where the real fights are happening: in state capitols, in communities deciding whether to host data centers, and, as we’ve seen this past week, in the markets watching the AI boom. J.B. Branch, director of federal AI governance and technology policy at Public Citizen, a nonprofit advocacy group that describes itself as nonpartisan, told me that the tech industry “realizes they have an optics problem.” He characterized moves like the Schumer hire and the rebranding as “PR washing.” He expects more of it, too, pointing to OpenAI’s partnership with the American Federation of Teachers, announced last year, as well as Anthropic’s newly launched Claude Corps and Meta’s America’s Workforce Academy. “I would imagine more of that sort of investment in these corporate, private-public partnerships,” he said. These initiatives didn’t spring up overnight. Meta and other tech companies reportedly began looking for ways to strengthen their ties to Democrats as Democratic gains in the midterms looked more likely. Reached for comment about the midterm elections’ impact on Meta, a company spokesperson pointed TechCrunch to remarks that Meta President Dina Powell McCormick made this week at WSJ Tech. “You have to work with the government that the American people elect,” McCormick had said. “I have seen it across the board that you have to be bipartisan, and you want to be, because you want buy-in on the things that you’re trying to do.” Not everyone expects them to work. Alice Marwick, director of research at the tech policy nonprofit Data & Society, told me she expects Big Tech to try to pivot back toward the middle, “if not the left. But it’s a little too late,” she said. “Tech companies should be asking themselves how their products can make people’s lives better, because right now, it doesn’t seem like they are.” If Democrats follow through on pledges to tighten oversight of AI and Big Tech, the industry could face a tougher environment. Data center moratoriums are gaining traction, and a wave of AI regulation bills awaits drafting. At the same event, Powell McCormick said Meta wants to show that communities welcoming its investments will see “an enormous amount of benefit,” while those that don’t want them “will of course have the right to stop them.” Still, the next two years could bring political gridlock in Washington. Aryan Ranjan, founder of Baraza, a political campaign management software company, told me most action will likely happen at the state level, since states have already sued tech companies and passed regulations. “A coalition built on newer, working-class voters is likely to push Democrats to frame AI around electricity bills, data-center siting and jobs rather than abstract AI safety,” he said of what to expect at the federal level. Last December, the Trump administration signed an executive order creating the AI Litigation Task Force , a federal group meant to challenge state AI laws. The administration has argued that U.S. AI companies “must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulations.” Many states have nonetheless passed their own laws, including measures on chatbots and deepfakes. It also remains to be seen how President Trump will respond, including whether he’ll sign more AI executive orders or veto bills that could be seen as anti-AI. Clearly, voters want stronger guardrails around the technology. In a statement to TechCrunch, a White House official said: “American leadership in super intelligence is essential for our national security, economic prosperity, and the quality of life of the American people. President Trump is committed to ensuring America continues to lead the world in super intelligence while protecting American consumers. As the President has said, he’s willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.” Branch argued that Trump’s political fortunes are now tied to the AI industry. On Wednesday, the day after the midterms, a trillion-dollar market sell-off spooked investors, some are whom are reportedly now reconsidering Anthropic’s reported trillion-dollar IPO. “There’s a very strong likelihood that there will be an AI bubble pop, and it’ll happen on Trump’s hands,” Branch said, predicting a possible market collapse. “Does he want to sink or swim along with the AI industry?”

articles.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
articles.body_text: Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion , confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management. Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity. Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, but it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus. The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development. Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. The deal to sell the site to Google was first reported by Bloomberg in June, but the Wyoming setback didn’t stop Crusoe from raising a $3.9 billion round in September. Crusoe makes money by leasing data center space to customers that bring their own GPUs, by renting out its own GPUs, and by selling compute power used to run AI models, known as inference. Crusoe’s largest projects serve some of the biggest names in AI. Its campus in Abilene, Texas, is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and the company is also constructing a separate 900-megawatt campus next door for Microsoft, with its first building expected to come online in mid-2027. Meta is also a customer, and Bloomberg reported that the trading firm Jane Street signed a $13 billion , five-year cloud deal with Crusoe. Crusoe was founded by Chase Lochmiller, now its CEO, and Cully Cavness, who started it as a cryptocurrency-mining business powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been burned off. In September, alongside its $3.9 billion funding round, the company added three board members , including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. Crusoe later became the first customer of Straubel’s energy-storage business. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission .
